# Introduction

## Project Background

Sino Yoga is a yoga and wellness brand built around **Five-Element Meridian Yoga**. It integrates Traditional Chinese Medicine concepts with yoga practice.

-   Core brand promise: holistic healing for mind, body, and energy.

-   Digital growth is centered on YouTube content.

-   The channel has an established base, but engagement must become more consistent.

    ![](images/Screenshot%202026-04-10%20151956-01.png)

## Problem Statement

Sino Yoga has valuable content, but the channel shows signs of **inconsistent audience engagement**: an early visibility spike, lower ongoing interaction, and uneven performance across videos

## Analytics Objective

-   Evaluate viewer commitment on Sino Yoga’s YouTube channel.
-   Identify top-performing content formats and themes.
-   Translate performance patterns into a data-driven content strategy.

## Importance

The channel can attract attention, but audience engagement must be strengthened so viewers return, interact, and follow a structured content journey.

**Outcome expected**

-   Stronger retention and repeat viewing.
-   Clearer content pillars.
-   Playlists and series that move viewers from passive watching to active participation.

# Literature Review

## Existence of well-established consumer behavior theory/models

-   **Customer engagement theory** - treats engagement as a multidimensional relationship between consumer and brand, not just a click or view [@brodie2011].\
-   **Social media engagement theory** - emphasizes cognitive, emotional, and behavioral engagement in digital environments [@digangi2016].\
-   **Branded YouTube content strategy** - suggests that content planning should consider platform behavior, publishing consistency, and audience value [@wang2020].\
-   **Customer journey thinking** - helps position engagement as the middle stage between discovery and later conversion [@lemon2016].

## Assessment of adequateness of gathered data

1.  The data is adequate for **descriptive analytics**: which months and videos performed best.
2.  The data is partly adequate for **diagnostic analytics**: engagement rates can flag where reach did not become interaction.
3.  The data is not fully adequate for **predictive analytics** without viewer-level variables, retention curves, and survey responses.

## Need for additional analysis

**Add platform data**

-   Retention curves
-   Average percentage viewed by video type
-   Returning-viewer behavior
-   Comment sentiment

**Add audience data**

-   Survey content preferences
-   Yoga experience level
-   Motivation for watching
-   Preferred video length and format

# Methods

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)
library(gt)
library(plotly)
library(glue)

monthly_raw <- read_excel("Sino Yoga monthy data.xlsx", sheet = "monthy data") |> 
  clean_names()

videos_raw <- read_excel("lifetime download with translations.xlsx", sheet = "Table data") |> 
  clean_names()

monthly <- monthly_raw |>
  mutate(
    month = ym(date),
    across(
      any_of(c(
        "subscribers", "videos_added", "videos_published", "impressions",
        "new_viewers", "returning_viewers", "likes", "dislikes", "shares",
        "comments_added", "views", "watch_time_hours", "estimated_revenue_usd"
      )),
      as.numeric
    ),
    engagement_actions = replace_na(likes, 0) + replace_na(shares, 0) + replace_na(comments_added, 0),
    engagement_rate = engagement_actions / views,
    returning_viewer_share = returning_viewers / (new_viewers + returning_viewers),
    avg_view_duration_min = period_to_seconds(hms(average_view_duration)) / 60
  ) |>
  arrange(month)

videos <- videos_raw |>
  filter(!str_detect(str_to_upper(coalesce(video_title_2, "")), "TOTAL")) |>
  mutate(
    across(
      any_of(c(
        "views", "likes", "shares", "subscribers", "watch_time_hours",
        "impressions", "engaged_views", "average_percentage_viewed_percent",
        "impressions_click_through_rate_percent", "estimated_revenue_usd"
      )),
      as.numeric
    ),
    publish_date = parse_date_time(
      video_publish_time,
      orders = c(
        "Ymd HMS", "Ymd HM", "Ymd",
        "ymd HMS", "ymd HM", "ymd",
        "mdY HMS", "mdY HM", "mdY",
        "mdy HMS", "mdy HM", "mdy",
        "B d, Y", "b d, Y"
      )
    ) |> as.Date(),
    engagement_rate = (replace_na(likes, 0) + replace_na(shares, 0)) / views,
    title_short = str_trunc(video_title, 70)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(views), views > 0)

n_months <- nrow(monthly)
n_videos <- nrow(videos)
total_views <- sum(monthly$views, na.rm = TRUE)
total_likes <- sum(monthly$likes, na.rm = TRUE)
total_shares <- sum(monthly$shares, na.rm = TRUE)
total_comments <- sum(monthly$comments_added, na.rm = TRUE)

top_video <- videos |> 
  slice_max(views, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

top_video_share <- top_video$views / sum(videos$views, na.rm = TRUE)

avg_monthly_engagement <- mean(monthly$engagement_rate, na.rm = TRUE)

monthly_long <- monthly |>
  select(month, likes, shares, comments_added, subscribers) |>
  pivot_longer(-month, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      comments_added = "Comments",
      likes = "Likes",
      shares = "Shares",
      subscribers = "Subscribers"
    )
  )

top_videos <- videos |>
  arrange(desc(views)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number())
```

## Data wrangling

```{r}
#| label: wrangling-code
#| echo: true
#| results: hide
monthly <- read_excel("Sino Yoga monthy data.xlsx", sheet = "monthy data") |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    month = ym(date),
    engagement_actions = likes + shares + comments_added,
    engagement_rate = engagement_actions / views,
    returning_viewer_share = returning_viewers / (new_viewers + returning_viewers)
  ) |>
  arrange(month)

videos <- read_excel("lifetime download with translations.xlsx", sheet = "Table data") |>
  clean_names() |>
  filter(!str_detect(str_to_upper(coalesce(video_title_2, "")), "TOTAL")) |>
  mutate(
    engagement_rate = (replace_na(likes, 0) + replace_na(shares, 0)) / views,
    title_short = str_trunc(video_title, 70)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(views), views > 0)
```

## Sample characteristics

**Monthly sample**

-   Unit of analysis: month
-   Period covered: `r format(min(monthly$month), "%b %Y")` to `r format(max(monthly$month), "%b %Y")`
-   Sample size: `r n_months` monthly observations

**Video sample**

-   Unit of analysis: YouTube video
-   Sample size: `r n_videos` non-total videos
-   Used for top-video and engagement-rate analysis

## Measures

| Construct | Operational Measure | Role in AO2 |
|----|---:|----|
| Reach | Views, impressions | Shows exposure |
| Engagement actions | Likes + shares + comments | Captures active response |
| Engagement rate | Engagement actions / views | Normalizes interaction quality |
| Retention proxy | Average view duration, average % viewed | Indicates viewer commitment |
| Loyalty proxy | Returning viewer share, subscribers gained | Indicates repeat connection |

## Analytics methods

-   **Descriptive analytics:** summarize monthly views, engagement actions, engagement rate, watch time, and subscriber growth.
-   **Top-content analysis:** rank videos by views and compare reach with likes/shares.
-   **Engagement quality analysis:** compare engagement rate and average percentage viewed to identify content that performs beyond reach.
-   **Future predictive plan:** use regression or clustering when survey data and retention curves are available.

## Preliminary Results

Monthly Engagement Story

```{r}
#| label: monthly-plot
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-width: 9.5
monthly_plot <- ggplot(monthly, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = views, text = glue("Month: {format(month, '%b %Y')}<br>Views: {comma(views)}")),
            linewidth = 1.2, color = "#7A36B1") +
  geom_point(aes(y = views, text = glue("Month: {format(month, '%b %Y')}<br>Views: {comma(views)}")),
             size = 2.8, color = "#7A36B1") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b\n%Y", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly views show an early spike followed by softer performance",
    subtitle = "AO2 takeaway: content planning should focus on repeatable engagement, not one-time reach spikes.",
    x = NULL, y = "Views"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0))

ggplotly(monthly_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

Top Performing Videos

```{r}
#| label: top-table
top_videos |>
  transmute(
    Rank = rank,
    `Video title` = title_short,
    Views = views,
    Likes = likes,
    Shares = shares,
    `Engagement rate` = engagement_rate,
    `Avg. % viewed` = average_percentage_viewed_percent
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(Views, Likes, Shares), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = `Engagement rate`, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = `Avg. % viewed`, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Top 10 videos by views**"),
    subtitle = "Reach leaders for AO2 content planning"
  ) |>
  tab_options(table.width = pct(100))
```
